newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma bomb defense asks for suppression hearing.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma bomb defense asks for suppression hearing.

text.p: Lawyers for Oklahoma City bombing defendant Timothy McVeigh asked the trial judge to block the submission of handwriting identification evidence by prosecutors, according to court filings made public Tuesday.
"Handwriting identification evidence is no more reliable than astrology, palm readings or psychic readings," the attorneys said in the court filings.
"The fact that handwriting experts have been permitted to testify repeatedly in the past is no reason that they should be permitted to testify in the future," they said.
McVeigh's attorneys asked U.S. District Judge Richard Matsch to hold a suppression hearing, to block "bad science gone amok."
The defence attorneys also said evidence based on McVeigh's hair samples should be thrown out because such analysis is unreliable.
McVeigh and his former army buddy Terry Nichols have been charged in the April 1995 bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah federal building in Oklahoma City, which killed 168 people.
The two will be tried separately, with McVeigh's trial scheduled first, on March 31. Nichols' trial date has not yet been set.

In another development, McVeigh's attorneys are seeking prison tapes of phone calls that former friend Michael Fortier made to his wife Lori because the defence fears the two may have been collaborating on their testimony.

Michael Fortier, who is in prison, has entered into a plea agreement that requires him to testify against McVeigh. His wife Lori was given immunity from prosecution in exchange for her testimony, McVeigh's lawyers said.

"It is simply preposterous to believe that these two witnesses have not discussed the substance of their testimony in telephone conversations during Michael Fortier's incarceration," McVeigh's lawyers said.
